propositions: CPython 3.12+ warns about fork() deadlock risk when invoked from multithreaded hosts; the grounding harness hard-codes POSIX fork context which triggers this warning.

The default multiprocessing context must be switched from fork to spawn to be cross-platform safe and compatible with future Python versions; callers requiring fork must explicitly inject the context.
Worker callables must be importable module-level names with pickleable arguments, kwargs, and return values; dynamic closures and lambdas are no longer supported under spawn.
Process start failures, pickling failures, and parent receive/unpickling failures must return abstaining RunResult instead of propagating exceptions.
The public run_in_worker API must document the callable/serialization contract and the explicit fork escape hatch for informed legacy/frozen-executable compatibility.
